title: Reorder List
statement: You get the first node of a singly linked list L0, L1, ... Ln. Rearrange it in place into L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, L2, ... so the ends take turns. Change the links only, not the values. The function returns nothing.

example.caption: Take from the front, then the back, then the front again.

idea.sentence: A list cannot be read from the back, so split it in the middle, reverse the second half, and weave the two halves one node at a time.

jargon.plain: Two pointers walking the same list. Slow moves one node per turn, fast moves two. When fast reaches the end, slow is at the middle.
You relink the existing nodes. You do not build a new list or copy values.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the node values in order, e.g. [1,2,3,4,5]

compare.bruteLabel: Copy nodes into an array, then relink with two indexes

rows.name: Array of nodes
rows.note: Easy to write: indexes i and n-1-i. But it stores every node.

rows.name: Middle, reverse, weave
rows.note: Three passes, each linear. Only a handful of pointers.

fast.takeaway: Both are linear in time. The three-step version saves the array by reusing the list itself as the way to reach the back.

stages.title: Find the middle
stages.note: slow moves one node, fast moves two. When fast cannot go further, slow is at the end of the first half.

stages.title: Reverse the second half
stages.note: Cut the list after slow. Flip the arrows of the second half so its old tail comes first.

stages.title: Weave the halves
stages.note: Link one node from the first half, then one from the reversed half, and so on until the second half is used up.

edges.title: Empty list
edges.why: The guard returns at once. There is no head to touch.

edges.title: One or two nodes
edges.why: Already in the right order. The guard handles one node. For two, the weave links 1 to 2 and nothing changes.

edges.title: Odd length
edges.why: The middle node stays in the first half and ends the answer. The halves are 2 nodes and 1 node.

edges.title: Repeated values
edges.why: Values do not matter. You move nodes by position only.

gotchas.text: Cut the first half (slow.next = null) before you weave. Otherwise the last node of the first half still points into the second half and the list loops.
Save both next pointers (n1 and n2) before you relink. After first.next = second you can no longer reach the rest of the first half.
slow.next has the type ListNode | null, so slow = slow.next needs a ! or a check. It is safe here because fast stays ahead of slow.
The function returns void. Tests need the head after the call, so check the same head object you passed in, not a return value.
reorderList(head *ListNode) changes nodes through pointers, so the caller sees the result. Do not reassign head inside and expect the caller to notice.

recap.key: Slow/fast finds the middle. Reverse the second half. Then alternate nodes from the two halves.
moves: Weave: first.next = second, second.next = saved next
